newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais denies joint venture talk.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais denies joint venture talk.

text.p: French state bank Credit Lyonnais issued a statement on Thursday categorically denying any plans for a significant link-up with a U.S. bank.

The statement followed a report in French newspaper Les Echos which cited Credit Lyonnais' U.S. operations managing director Robert Cohen as saying joint ventures with a U.S. investment bank should be announced shortly.

"Following press information published this morning after an interview with Robert Cohen, Credit Lyonnais categorically denies any significant project with an American bank," said the statement issued from the state-owned bank's Paris headquarters.

"No creation of joint venture companies are under discusssion with a bank, American or other, concerning the group's North American activities, apart from possible specific projects concerning specific products," the statement said.
"No planned deal of considerable importance in the region is being studied," it said.
The comments from Robert Cohen, the outgoing head of Credit Lyonnais in New York, did no commit the group, it said.
However, a Credit Lyonnais spokesman said he could confirm the profit figures Cohen gave to Les Echos.
Les Echos said Cohen told it the U.S. Credit Lyonnais arm was "doing better than ever" and had produced a net profit of $211 million in 1996, up 40 percent on the previous year.
Cohen is due to join Rebublic National Bank.
